subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI resolve disruptive scroll jumps by fixing renderer/viewport anchoring by default, by adding an explicit TUI auto-scroll mode, or by waiting for the narrower pi-tui scrollback-clearing work to land first?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the right durable fix crosses terminal UX policy, third-party renderer ownership, and possible settings/config surface rather than being a narrow code-only repair.

options.title: Repair renderer and anchor behavior
options.body: Prefer a default-on fix that stops content-driven redraws or in-place streaming updates from disrupting the viewport, with a live PTY proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll setting
options.body: Expose explicit user control only if maintainers want a new terminal preference and are willing to own fresh-install and upgrade behavior for that setting.

options.title: Hold for narrow dependency fix
options.body: Keep this issue open while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78017 or an upstream pi-tui patch proves the renderer root cause is solved, then re-evaluate remaining TUI viewport behavior.

recommendation.title: Repair renderer and anchor behavior
recommendation.body: Prefer a default-on fix that stops content-driven redraws or in-place streaming updates from disrupting the viewport, with a live PTY proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-routing signal for TUI state/rendering paths from local blame and recent merged TUI fixes.
